title: Bias-Spectrum Neural Processes for Parametric PDEs: Architecture Priors Meet PDE Constraints
claim: Inductive biases lie on a spectrum from weak structural to strong physical priors, and principled mechanisms integrate them across it.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right gradient spectrum, with dashed arrows to bottom mechanism boxes
description: A wide diagram with a blue-to-red horizontal gradient band that represents inductive bias strength. A thick dark arrow labeled 'Inductive Bias Strength' runs left to right. On the left, under the blue header 'Weak Structural Priors', four blue-outlined boxes are stacked: Translation Equivariance, Permutation Invariance, Locality & Smoothness, and Coverage Awareness. Each has an italic subtitle such as 'Convolutional layers' or 'Set-based encoders'. On the right, under the red header 'Strong Physical Priors', three red-outlined boxes are stacked: PDE Residual, Boundary Conditions and Conservation Laws. The first two carry equations (G_λ[u]=0 and B_λ[u]=0). Two green boxes sit at the bottom center: Stochastic Collocation and Mean-Field Enforcement, each with three bullets. Dashed green curved arrows run from the red boxes down to the green boxes. A gray banner at the bottom reads 'Principled Mechanisms for Cross-Spectrum Bias Integration'. The eye goes first to the gradient and arrow, then to the green mechanism boxes.
caption: The inductive bias spectrum for parametric PDEs.
abstract: Parametric partial differential equations (PDEs) serve as fundamental models across science and engineering, yet constructing fast and accurate surrogate models from sparse, irregularly sampled observations with reliable uncertainty quantification remains challenging. Existing approaches struggle to simultaneously handle variable observation patterns, preserve physics consistency, and provide well-calibrated predictive uncertainty. We introduce Bias-Spectrum Neural Processes (BSNP), a unified meta-learning framework that systematically integrates weak structural priors (translation equivariance, locality) with strong physical priors (governing equations and boundary conditions). BSNP addresses two critical obstacles: discretization overfitting through stochastic collocation that resamples residual evaluation points, and uncertainty collapse through mean-field enforcement that applies PDE constraints only to predictive means while preserving learned uncertainty. Comprehensive experiments on nonlinear Poisson equations, Burgers dynamics, and Navier-Stokes flows demonstrate that BSNP achieves superior accuracy and well-calibrated uncertainty quantification in sparse-data regimes.
